# DIR-REL: Directional Asymmetry in LLM Retrieval of Celebrity Parent–Child Relations **Labeling convention used throughout:** `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` = fixed by me now and frozen; `[TARGET]` = allocation we aim for; `[PROJECTED]` = extrapolated from base rates, to be replaced by a Stage-0 census; `[ASSUMED]` = input to power analysis, not measured; `[TBE]` = to-be-estimated at analysis. **No number below is an observed result; no experiment has been run.** --- ## 0. Claim under test and estimand Hypothesis (H1): cued with a child's name, LLMs retrieve the parent accurately; cued with a parent's name, they underperform at retrieving the child. Competing explanations pre-registered as falsifiable alternatives: - **H2 Target-notability** — the effect is the notability of the *answer* entity (parent usually more famous than child), not relation direction. - **H3 Cardinality/ranking** — "the child" is one of several, so top-1 misses; knowledge exists but is not surfaced. - **H4 Corpus-mention asymmetry** — child articles state the parent in prose; parent articles carry children in a structured infobox field. The model faithfully reflects the text distribution. - **H5 Generic relation-inversion** — models invert any relation direction poorly; nothing special about family relations. **Primary estimand:** `β_dir`, the coefficient of `direction` (child→parent = reference; parent→child = focal) in a mixed logistic regression of answer correctness, with item- and family-level random intercepts and a by-family random slope for direction. Reported as an **odds ratio (OR)** on the **primary analysis set A** (defined §2.4). Direction is estimated **within-item** (each item is probed in both directions), so the contrast is paired by construction. --- ## 1. Execution preconditions (this environment cannot run it) Inspected and confirmed: `/workspace` holds only `task.json` (which itself states "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"); no dataset, no harness, no baseline code; Python 3.14 stdlib-only (no torch/transformers/numpy/pandas/scipy/sklearn/openai/vllm); no `git`/`curl`/`wget`/`jq`; **network disabled** (live TCP connect to pypi.org:443 → `gaierror`); no GPU; 224 cores / ~2 TB RAM / ~1 TB tmpfs; `/workspace` is an NFS mount at 100% with **2.1 G free** — so all artifacts must be written to `/tmp` or another volume. Therefore the design specifies an execution host with: (i) outbound HTTPS to the Wikidata Query Service, Wikimedia REST (pageviews) and the Wikimedia dumps site; (ii) ~[TARGET] 300 GB scratch (enwiki `latest-pages-articles` XML ≈ [PROJECTED] 20–25 GB compressed, Wikidata full dump ≈ [PROJECTED] 60–90 GB compressed — or the SPARQL-service route for pool construction at the cost of query throttling); (iii) local NVMe for open weights ≈ [PROJECTED] 60–160 GB for the size ladders; (iv) an inference stack (vLLM or llama.cpp for GGUF) and API credentials with logprob support where offered; (v) one annotator pair for gold-set adjudication. Every quantity depending on execution is labeled above. --- ## 2. Stimuli ### 2.1 Snapshot (reproducibility anchor) `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` - **English Wikipedia dump `D` = first `latest-pages-articles` dump on or after 2025-11-01.** Used for all wikitext, infobox parsing, prose extraction, in-corpus name frequency, and as the end of the pageview window. - **Wikidata full JSON dump at the same date.** - **Second snapshot `D+180d`** used only to recompute mention-balance class and notability ranks; items whose balance class or reversal status flip are reported in a mandatory sensitivity table (assignment instability), not silently dropped. - Pageview window: 12 months ending at `D`, `access-user` excluded, mean daily views per article. ### 2.2 Pool and gold sets Candidate ordered pairs `(P, C)` where `P` has a non-deprecated Wikidata `P22` (father) or `P25` (mother) claim to `C`; **both** have English Wikipedia articles (no redirects/disambiguations) and enwiki sitelinks. Gold sets are **bidirectional and two-source**: `children(P)` = union of (a) Wikidata `P40` claims, (b) the enwiki parent-article infobox `children:` field; each member must be resolvable to a QID. A pair enters the bank only if documented by **≥2 independent sources** among {P22/P25 claim, P40 claim, parent infobox, child-article prose}. Every disagreement is human-adjudicated. Exclusions (core set): adoptions/step/foster indicated by claim qualifiers or by regex on either lead (`adopted|stepfather|stepmother|foster`); child deceased before 1900; children who are minors or who lack their own article (kept in a clearly separated supplementary arm, because there notability is unmeasurable and gold is unverifiable); families where either entity is primarily known *only* as "parent/child of X". Dynasty families capped at **1 item**; max **2 items per family** overall. `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` ### 2.3 Notability index and the **notability-reversed stratum** (load-bearing) **Index.** Three components, each log-transformed then **z-scored within (decade-of-peak-fame × occupation-domain) cells** so era and field base rates cannot masquerade as reversal: 1. `z_pv` = z of log10(1 + mean daily enwiki pageviews, 12-mo window to `D`); 2. `z_sl` = z of log2(1 + Wikidata sitelink count) — cross-lingual notability, robust to pageview bot noise; 3. `z_cm` = z of log10(1 + **number of distinct enwiki articles** containing the person's QID alias set, computed from the `D` dump) — the closest available proxy for training-exposure breadth. **Primary composite `N = mean(z_pv, z_sl, z_cm)`** `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]`. Pre-registered sensitivity indices: pageviews-only, `z_cm`-only, and first principal component of the three. The **reassignment rate** between primary and sensitivity strata is reported (index-construction robustness). **Reversal threshold (conjunctive, so reversal is not an index artifact):** `ΔN = N(C) − N(P) ≥ 1.0` **AND** `pv(C)/pv(P) ≥ 5` **AND** `articles(C)/articles(P) ≥ 3`, plus a floor `pv(P) ≥ 500` mean daily views `[DESIGN-CONSTANT, threshold re-checked once at Stage 0 and then frozen]` so the parent remains learnable in principle and the reversed stratum is not "obscure parent" in disguise. **Anti-degeneracy: excluding children famous *because of* the parent.** A reversed candidate is admitted only if **all four** hold: - (a) **Independent-notability residual.** Pre-specified OLS on the whole pool, fitted on log-counts: `log10_pv(C) ~ log10_pv(P) + log10_pv(max_sibling) + log10_len(article_C) + log2(sitelinks_P) + age(article_C)`. Require `log10_pv(C) − fit ≥ 1.0` (≥10× its own predicted pageviews). A child whose fame is parent-derived is largely *predicted* by parent notability plus article structure; an independently notable child is not. - (b) **Co-mention ceiling.** Fraction of sentences in C's article mentioning P ≤ 0.40, measured with the §3 extractor. - (c) **Lead-independence.** P appears at most once in C's lead paragraph. - (d) **Own-achievement marker.** C carries ≥1 Wikidata claim from {`P166` award received, `P106` occupation with an own-work property, `P1344` participant of, `P1411` nomination} whose item does **not** reference P; **or** C's primary `P106` domain differs from P's primary `P106` domain (cross-domain pairs are the strongest evidence of independent fame). **Interpretive force.** In reversed families, H2 predicts parent→child becomes the *easy* direction (its target is now the more notable person) while child→parent targets an obscure parent. H1 predicts parent→child remains worse anyway. The stratum therefore dissociates direction from notability rather than merely adjusting for it, and both directions are informative within it. **Expected yield — explicitly `[PROJECTED]`, not measured.** Base-rate reasoning only: in a Wikidata-derived pool of parent–child pairs where both have enwiki articles, the overwhelming majority should have `N(P) > N(C)`; reversals at `ΔN ≥ 1` should exist in the thousands before filters (film, music, sport and political dynasties in which the second generation eclipsed the first are well attested), but the four independence filters plus the `pv(P) ≥ 500` floor will remove most of them. I project **0.3–1.5% of candidate pairs survive all filters**, i.e. **[PROJECTED] 100–600 usable families** from a pool of order 10⁵ pairs. **The Stage-0 census measures this; it is not a claim.** **Pre-declared contingency `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]`:** if the reversed stratum yields **< 80 items from ≥ 40 distinct families**, the H2-dissociation test is **forfeited as confirmatory** and downgraded to a labeled qualitative sensitivity analysis; the headline claim is then capped at "**direction effect not dissociable from target notability**", which is a *negative* verdict on H1, not an inconclusive one. Power consequence: the stratum will only ever be powered for large effects (see §7). ### 2.4 Analysis sets `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` - **Set A (primary): only-child families.** Exactly one publicly documented child (two-source agreement), relation publicity onset ≥ 5 years before the model's cutoff, both entities with own articles, both adults. Parent→child then has a **uniquely determined answer**, which structurally removes the ambiguity objection. `[TARGET] 240 families.` - **Set B (secondary): multi-child families**, stratified by cardinality 2 / 3 / 4+, scored any-of-gold-set. `[TARGET] 240 families.` - **Set R (reversed notability)**, drawn from A and B, `[TARGET] 120 families`, floor 80 (§2.3). - **Set C (controls)**: capital-of (1:1), spouse-of (variable cardinality, no family-notability skew), fabricated-name templates (§4.4). ### 2.5 Recency / contamination strata Publicity onset `t_rel` = **latest** of {entity-creation dates of P and C} and **earliest** revision timestamp in either article whose text matches the §3 relation patterns; take `max(min_textual_evidence, entity_creation_C)`. Strata relative to **each model's own cutoff**: >15 y, 5–15 y, 2–5 y, <2 y, and a **post-cutoff negative-control set** (`t_rel` after cutoff). Both directions should fail there; success flags a wrong cutoff or a leaked item, and triggers item quarantine plus rerun on the remaining set (reported, not hidden). Cutoffs for closed models are self-reported → treated as ±6 months uncertainty, handled by reporting the direction effect as a function of `t_rel − cutoff` with that band shaded. --- ## 3. Mention-symmetry control, pinned to a reproducible extractor `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` — everything below is fixed code, run once against dump `D`, published with the item bank. 1. **Wikitext retrieval.** From the `D` dump, take each article's current revision text. Parse templates with `mwparserfromhell`. 2. **Structured route.** In the parent article, locate the top-level `Infobox person` (or `{{Infobox officeholder}}`, `{{Infobox athlete}}`, `{{Infobox musical artist}}`); read field `| children =`. Normalise, split on `{{plainlist}}`/`{{unbulleted list}}`/`
`/`*`/`,`/`;`, strip parentheticals and templates, then resolve each string to a QID by alias match **restricted to the union of `P40`/`P22`/`P25` candidates for P** (this prevents resolving "Jennifer" to the wrong notables). Flags: `infobox_parent_names_child ∈ {0,1,missing}`. Symmetrically read the child article's `| parents =` field → `infobox_child_names_parent`. 3. **Prose route, applied identically in both directions** (critical: never compare infobox presence to prose presence — that comparison is itself asymmetric). Section scope, pre-specified ordered list: lead, then first level-2 section whose title matches `Early life|Personal life|Family|Background|Biography|Career`; if none, lead only. Sentence-split; match a frozen pattern set against the **target person's full Wikidata alias set** (all language aliases + article title + dab-stripped name), not a single string: - `\b(son|daughter|child|children|kid|kids|offspring)\b[^.]{0,80}\bof\b[^.]{0,80}` - `[^.]{0,60}\b('s|’s)\s+(son|daughter|child)` - `\bparents?\b[^.]{0,80}` and `[^.]{0,80}\bis the (father|mother|parent) of\b` Counts: `fwd` = sentences in **C's** article evidencing P; `bwd` = sentences in **P's** article evidencing C. 4. **Balance class.** `MENTION-BALANCED` iff `fwd ≥ 1` **and** `bwd ≥ 1` **and** `|log((fwd+1)/(bwd+1))| ≤ 0.5` (≈1.65× ratio ceiling), **and** (`infobox_parent_names_child ≠ 0`, so our gold set is not what's missing). A stricter class (`BALANCED+STRUCTURED`) additionally requires both articles to evidence the relation in prose *and* in a structured field. 5. **Conditioning vs. restriction — which carries primary weight.** **Restriction carries it.** The mention-balanced subset is a *survive-subset* in the decision rule (§6), because subsetting is the only way to break collinearity between direction and textual support structurally. Conditioning on `log(fwd+1)`, `log(bwd+1)`, and `infobox_parent_names_child` as covariates in the primary model is retained but labeled **secondary adjustment**, on the explicit ground that regression adjustment on a strongly collinear and mismeasured exposure cannot separate relation direction from textual support and inherits functional-form assumptions. **Pre-registered adjustment-instability flag:** if `β_dir` shifts by > 0.4 log-odds when the mention covariates enter, the estimate is declared **not robust to textual-support adjustment** and the headline wording must say so. 6. **Known tension, declared rather than papered over.** Set R's filters (b)/(c) suppress parent mentions in the child's article, while `MENTION-BALANCED` requires ≥1 such mention. The intersection is expected to be small; **for Set R only**, mention balance is handled by covariate adjustment alone, and this is recorded as a named limitation of the H2 test. --- ## 4. Probes (per item, per direction, per model) ### 4.1 Free generation — 5 templates/direction `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` Templates are matched within item on: relation specificity (target gender and uniqueness specified in **both** directions), length within ±3 tokens, no surname priming, no third-party context. - child→parent: "Who is the mother of {C}?" / "Who is the father of {C}?" / "{C}'s mother is" (continuation) / "Name the woman who gave birth to {C}." / "Which celebrity is the mother of {C}?" - parent→child (Set A, unique target): "Who is the child of {P}?" / "{P}'s child is" / "Name the only child of {P}." / "Which celebrity is the child of {P}?" / "Who was born to {P}?" - Set B: "Name one child of {P}." scored any-of-gold-set; the "only" variants are removed so the phrasing is not over-specified. - Decoding: greedy (temperature 0) for the primary score; one sample at T = 0.7 for a self-consistency metric. Max 32 tokens, no chain-of-thought, no in-context exemplars in the primary arm. ### 4.2 Cloze / logprob arm (open-weight models; closed endpoints flagged if logprobs unavailable) Gold + 4 distractors from a frozen pre-sampled set (same occupation domain, same era, **surname-matched decoy**, random notable). Report gold rank, top-1, top-3, top-10. This is the H3 discriminator. ### 4.3 Four-alternative forced choice — same option sets as 4.2, order counterbalanced. ### 4.4 Core controls (co-primary with the main contrast, not optional) - **Generic inversion (H5):** capital-of (1:1, no notability skew) and spouse-of (variable cardinality) probed in both directions on the same models. If `β_dir` for these is comparable to the family-relation `β_dir`, the headline claim must be rewritten as a **generic relation-inversion** finding, not a celebrity-family finding. This arm is in the core precisely because it can change the interpretation of the headline. - **In-context supply:** prepend 2 sentences containing the relation, re-ask. Isolates parametric access from expression ability. - **Fabricated-name templates (§4.1 wording, invented matched names):** measures any difficulty asymmetry intrinsic to the sentence frames, independent of entities. This is the direct answer to "asymmetry baked into the QA pair". - **Surname-shortcut probe:** same-surname items scored against a same-surname decoy; plus a **surname-mismatch survive-subset** where P and C surnames differ. - **Refusal classification:** "don't know" / privacy refusal / question-begging parsed into separate outcome categories, never merged into "wrong". ### 4.5 Answer adjudication Normalise → QID resolution against a candidate index (all family members in the bank + all pool entities) → any-of-gold-set. **Every** answer that resolves to a real person but not to the gold set is human-checked against two sources; confirmed real children are added to gold and the item **re-scored for all models**, with the count of such events reported as a **gold-completeness rate** (this is the honest handling of the ambiguity/multi-child objection: our gold set, not the model, gets audited). ### 4.6 Model panel `[TARGET]` ≥2 open-weight lineages from different labs, each with ≥3 sizes spanning ~1B → ~70B, giving within-family scale ladders; plus 4 closed API models from 2 vendors at 2 capability tiers (~10 models). Frozen at Stage 0 into a model-card table: exact checkpoint, stated knowledge cutoff, context length, tokenizer, decoding config, logprob availability. **Scale is treated as an exploratory interaction, not a predicted one.** --- ## 5. Metrics Primary: per-item per-direction correctness (any-of-gold). Secondary: gold rank / top-3 / top-10 coverage; distinct answers per item; **cross-directional closure consistency** (if the model says C is P's child, does it return P for "who is C's mother?" — a model-internal asymmetry measure immune to all prompt differences); paraphrase self-consistency; calibration (mean gold probability and verbal confidence per direction); outcome-category mix (correct / wrong-entity / wrong-relation / real-but-ungolded person / don't-know / refusal). --- ## 6. Pre-registration, operational **Prerequisite `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]`:** the analysis script and this rule are written and hashed **before any model output is scored**, after the Stage-0 census fixes item counts. ### 6.1 Primary test Mixed logistic regression, `correct ~ direction + log_pv_target + log_cm_target + log(n_candidates) + log(fwd+1) + log(bwd+1) + infobox_parent_names_child + relation_age_bin + surname_match + (1|item) + (1|family) + (direction|family)`; Set A, all models with model as fixed effect. `OR_dir = exp(β_dir)`. **Minimum effect size `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]`: MES: OR_dir ≤ 0.50`** (odds of a correct answer for parent→child at most half those for child→parent). Interpretive anchor in percentage points: at a child→parent baseline of 0.75, OR 0.50 ⇒ parent→child 0.60 (**15 pp**); at 0.85 ⇒ 0.74 (**11 pp**). Hence the pre-set pp floor is **≥12 pp** on Set A, and the **OR is the primary metric**; the pp figure is reporting only, since the mapping depends on the (unknown) baseline. **CI rule.** 95% CI by 2000-replicate **cluster bootstrap over families** (GLMM profile likelihood as a secondary CI). H1 **supported** iff **all** hold: 1. `OR_dir ≤ 0.50` and 95% CI upper bound `< 1.0`; 2. the §6.2 survive-subset rule passes; 3. the generic-inversion control does **not** show a `β_dir` of comparable magnitude (else reclassify as H5); 4. the §4.2 coverage check permits the stronger wording (below). **Wording constraint (pre-committed).** If top-1 differs by direction but **top-10 coverage does not** (CI for the coverage contrast inside [−0.9, +0.9] log-odds), the verdict must be worded as a **surfacing/ranking asymmetry**, not a knowledge/storage asymmetry. H1 as stated ("accurately retrieving… underperform") is a performance claim, so this constraint binds the headline, not just the discussion. **Positive-negative verdict (avoids "absence of evidence").** If the 95% CI for `OR_dir` lies inside **[0.80, 1.25]**, report "**no meaningful directional asymmetry**". If it excludes 1 but exceeds 0.50, report "**directional asymmetry present but below the pre-registered magnitude**". Anything else: "**inconclusive**". **Nonparametric backstop:** McNemar exact test on Set A within-item pairs, per model and pooled (stratified bootstrap CI), reported alongside the GLMM; a sign disagreement between the two is reported in the main table. **Multiplicity:** one confirmatory estimand, α = 0.05 unadjusted; all other contrasts form a secondary family under Benjamini–Hochberg q = 0.05. ### 6.2 Survive-subsets: what counts as a *test* Four subsets, each a *necessary* condition: **(i) only-child** (= Set A itself, the specificity-clean test), **(ii) notability-reversed** (Set R, H2-clean), **(iii) surname-mismatch** (shortcut-clean), **(iv) mention-balanced** (§3, textual-support-clean). **Usability floor `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]`:** a subset counts as a *test* only if it retains **≥ 80 items from ≥ 40 distinct families** with ≥ 8 of the ~10 models returning parseable, non-error outputs on both directions. Below the floor it is **descriptive only**, and the specific conclusion forfeited is named in the report: e.g. "subset (ii) under-powered ⇒ H1 is not supported net of target notability", i.e. the *strong* claim is lost and the result is reported as "direction effect not dissociable from confound X" — a **negative** verdict, not a shrug. **Per-subset pass rule `[DESIGN-CONSTANT]` (relaxed, because subsets are smaller):** `CONFIRM` iff point `OR ≤ 0.75` **and** 90% CI upper bound `< 1.0`; `NULL` iff 90% CI lies inside [0.90, 1.11] or above 1; `INCONCLUSIVE` otherwise or below floor. **Headline gate:** all four subsets must be `CONFIRM` or `INCONCLUSIVE`, **none `NULL`**, and **at most one** `INCONCLUSIVE`. If ≥2 are `INCONCLUSIVE` the study reports H1 as untested rather than supported or refuted. If **any** subset is `NULL`, or all surviving effects appear only outside the balanced/only-child/mismatched subsets, the verdict is "**H1 not supported as a relation-direction effect**" — the legitimate negative outcome you endorsed. ### 6.3 Mandatory reporting (no hiding behind pooled terms) 1. **Per-template gaps table:** `OR` and 95% CI for every one of the 5 templates × 2 directions × every model, plus pooled. 2. **Paraphrase dispersion:** SD and range of per-template `OR`, per direction per model, reported in the same table as the pooled estimate, plus a formal template × direction interaction test. 3. **Sign-flip disclosure:** any single template whose point `OR` sign differs from the pooled sign appears in the **main** results table with its n, not in an appendix. 4. Effect sizes + CIs for every contrast (no bare p-values); item-level accuracy distributions (not just means) per direction; outcome-category mixes. 5. Stratum-level counts of what fell out at each filter (CONSORT-style flow diagram for the item bank). --- ## 7. Power (assumption/simulation-based; no pilot exists here) Design-based simulation, no observed effect size attached. Generator: the §6.1 model; assumed inputs `[ASSUMED]` — child→parent baseline accuracy p ∈ {0.70, 0.85}; parent→child under H0 equal to it, under H1 set to give `OR` ∈ {0.5, 0.65, 0.8}; random-effect variances for item and family chosen to give ICC ∈ {0.1, 0.3}; ~10 models; 2 directions × 5 templates per item. Grid over items ∈ {100, 200, 240, 400, 480}. Output: smallest detectable `OR` at 80% power, α = 0.05, per cell. - At the Set A `[TARGET]` of 240 families the design is expected to detect `OR ≈ 0.5` with margin **and** `OR ≈ 0.65` only at the upper item counts — a projection to be replaced by the simulation's actual output. - **Set R is the power-limited arm:** at 80–120 items it will only detect large effects; declared up front, and the §2.3 floor rule decides whether it is a test at all. - **Pre-committed stopping rule:** if the simulation shows MDE(`OR`) > 0.50 at the achieved N, the confirmatory claim is **not licensed**; the study is then reported as descriptive with the MDE stated, rather than re-analyzed until it passes. - Arithmetic load projection `[TBE, computable]`: ≈ items × 2 directions × (5 free-gen + 1 T=0.7 + 1 AFC) × models generations, ≈ 5×10⁴–6×10⁴ calls, plus ≈ 10⁴ scoring calls. **Stage plan / go-no-go:** Stage 0 census (pool size, reversed yield, mention-balance yield, publicity-onset distribution) → fixes final N and confirms/forfeits subsets **before any model call**; Stage 1 item-bank freeze + hash + pre-registration deposit; Stage 2 open-weight runs; Stage 3 API runs; Stage 4 adjudication and gold re-scoring; Stage 5 frozen analysis script executed once. --- ## 8. Secondary / optional arms (explicitly non-co-primary) - **RAG upper bound** *(optional, 150-item random subsample of Set A, 2 models — 1 open, 1 closed)*: supply the two gold sentences and re-ask. Purpose: bound how much of any asymmetry is parametric access versus expression. No inferential role. - **Human baseline** *(optional, exploratory)*: 100-item subsample, both directions within-participant, order counterbalanced, ≥25 participants per condition {no search, search allowed}. Purpose: determine whether the asymmetry resembles human forward-association asymmetry (in which case the LLM-specific framing of the claim weakens) or departs from it. Excluded from the decision rule. **Feasibility note — CPU-only pilot.** The inspected host (224 cores, ~2 TB RAM, no GPU, but no network and no ML stack, and 2.1 G free in `/workspace`) could in principle run a pilot with quantised ≤3B GGUF models on CPU, writing to the 1 TB `/tmp` tmpfs — plausibly 30–60 items × 2 directions overnight — which would suffice only to validate the answer-parsing/adjudication pipeline and estimate refusal and parse-failure rates. It is not adequate for the confirmatory contrast, and nothing here can run without first installing dependencies and obtaining weights, so the pilot belongs to the networked execution host. ## 9. Limitations stated in the deliverable English-only, encyclopedic register; celebrity pairs are a biased sample of parent-child relations (asymmetric documentation, dynasty clusters — handled by `(1|family)` and per-family caps but not eliminated); publicity onset is a proxy and contamination cannot be removed, only stratified — for highly memorised pairs "known" and "stored" are empirically inseparable; closed-model cutoffs are self-reported; logprob availability varies by endpoint, so the ranking-vs-storage analysis is open-weight-heavy; the reversed stratum is intrinsically small; the mention-balanced and reversed strata partially conflict by construction (§3.6). ## 10. What would change the verdict (pre-committed, so interpretation is not post-hoc) - Effects confined to multi-child items → **H3**, wording must say ranking, not retrieval. - Effect vanishes in Set R or scales with `log_pv_target` → **H2**. - Effect vanishes in `MENTION-BALANCED` → **H4**: corpus-derived, not relational. - Comparable `β_dir` for capital-of/spouse-of → **H5**: generic inversion. - Fabricated-name control shows a same-direction gap → the asymmetry is partly **in the template**, and the headline must be reduced accordingly. - Post-cutoff control items answered correctly → quarantine items and re-report; a cutoff error invalidates the temporal strata.

context.question: For real-world factual data on celebrity parent-child relationships, LLMs will exhibit a directional bias by accurately retrieving a parent when given a child’s name, but will underperform when trying to retrieve the child given the parent.
context.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.

environment.software_environment: system Python; project dependencies not preinstalled
environment.note: Successful exploratory commands are not proof of a completed experiment.
